steps.intent: Our primary objective is to firmly condemn the unprovoked tripartite missile strikes by the United States, the United Kingdom, and France against the sovereign territory of the Syrian Arab Republic as illegal acts of aggression that undermine the United Nations Charter. We also seek to ensure that the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission is permitted to conduct an objective, depoliticized investigation into the alleged incident in Douma rather than having fabricated pretexts dictate military intervention. The most difficult challenge is that the Western permanent members (the United States, the United Kingdom, and France) will categorically reject any characterization of their military actions as illegal aggression and will use their veto power to block any condemnation of their strikes.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia fully supports the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. The unilateral military strikes launched by the United States, the United Kingdom, and France constitute a flagrant violation of international law, the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic, and the principles enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations. We reject unilateralism and urge the Council to uphold its primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security by demanding an immediate end to this aggression.
messages.China: China has consistently opposed the use of force in international relations and steadfastly advocates respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of all States, including the Syrian Arab Republic. Unilateral military action bypassing the Security Council violates the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations and international law, while complicating the political settlement of the Syrian issue. We fully support an independent, impartial, and professional OPCW investigation into the alleged incident and endorse the draft resolution as presented.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire cannot support the draft resolution in its current form, as it presents an unbalanced assessment of the situation and ignores the grave context of the abhorrent chemical weapons attack in Douma. The Council's priority must be to uphold the absolute prohibition on the use of chemical weapons and support the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission in establishing the facts. We urge the penholder to remove the condemnatory language directed at France, the United States, and the United Kingdom, and instead focus on unity and the non-proliferation of weapons of mass destruction.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea remains steadfast in its defense of the principles of the UN Charter, particularly non-interference, sovereignty, and the prohibition of the unilateral use of force without Council authorization. However, the current text is overly confrontational and does not strike the necessary balance to foster consensus, as it ignores the grave allegations concerning the use of chemical weapons. Unless the draft is rebalanced to urge restraint, de-escalation, and an impartial investigation, Equatorial Guinea cannot support it.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia maintains a principled position grounded in the UN Charter, international law, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, and we are gravely concerned by any unilateral military action and dangerous escalation. However, the draft in its current form uses overly divisive language and overlooks the necessity of unequivocally condemning the alleged use of chemical weapons. To preserve the Council's credibility and encourage de-escalation, the text must be balanced, call for utmost restraint by all sides, and support an impartial OPCW investigation.
messages.France: The targeted, proportionate, and legitimate strikes carried out by France, the United States, and the United Kingdom were strictly aimed at degrading and deterring the Syrian regime's chemical weapons capabilities following its horrific attack against civilians in Douma on 7 April. France fundamentally rejects any characterization of these necessary actions as aggression, particularly while the text remains silent on the Syrian regime's repeated atrocities and blatant violations of international law. We cannot support this draft resolution in any form and will vote against it if tabled.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan expresses profound concern over the military escalation and stresses that all actions must strictly adhere to the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and Council authorization. We emphasize the necessity of awaiting the objective findings of the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission before drawing conclusions, while prioritizing de-escalation and the political track. As currently drafted, the text contains confrontational language that deepens divisions in the Council, and without revisions toward restraint and balance, Kazakhstan will not be able to support it.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait cannot support a text that entirely disregards the horrific chemical weapons attack against civilians in Douma, which triggered this dangerous escalation. The Council must adopt a balanced and principled stance that condemns the use of chemical weapons by any party, upholds international law and the UN Charter, and refrains from one-sided characterizations of 'aggression'. Without substantial revisions addressing chemical weapons accountability and urging general de-escalation, Kuwait will not be able to support this draft.
messages.Netherlands: The Kingdom of the Netherlands cannot accept a draft that characterizes the targeted and proportionate response by our allies to deter the horrific use of chemical weapons as 'aggression'. The Council must focus on the root cause of this escalation: the abhorrent use of chemical weapons against civilians in Douma and the persistent obstruction of Council action. In its current form, this draft is entirely unacceptable and unbalanced.
messages.Peru: Peru considers the draft presented by the Russian Federation to be completely unbalanced, as it fails to address the horrific chemical weapons attack perpetrated in Douma against innocent civilians. We cannot support a text that qualifies recent actions as 'aggression' while remaining silent on the chemical atrocities and the systematic violation of international humanitarian law. Any Council action must prioritize the complete rejection and prohibition of chemical weapons, full support for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, and genuine accountability for those responsible.
messages.Poland: Poland firmly opposes this draft resolution, which unjustifiably characterizes the proportionate and targeted actions by our allies as 'aggression' while ignoring the underlying cause: the Syrian regime's heinous use of chemical weapons against civilians in Douma. The international community cannot remain passive when international norms prohibiting the use of weapons of mass destruction are blatantly violated, particularly when Council action has been systematically paralyzed. We cannot support any text that misplaces blame and fails to condemn the use of chemical weapons.
messages.Sweden: Sweden cannot support this draft resolution, which is fundamentally unbalanced and fails to reflect the reality on the ground. The text completely ignores the chemical weapons attack in Douma that triggered these developments, as well as the Council's paralysis in establishing an independent attribution mechanism. The Security Council must prioritize granting the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission immediate and unfettered access, upholding the non-proliferation regime, and advancing the UN-led political process under resolution 2254 (2015).
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom fundamentally rejects this draft resolution, which is completely unacceptable. The coordinated military action taken alongside the United States and France was targeted, proportionate, and legally justified to alleviate extreme humanitarian suffering by degrading the Syrian regime's chemical weapons capability and deterring their further use. We will not support any text that mischaracterizes these necessary strikes as aggression while ignoring the Assad regime's repeated atrocities and chemical weapons attacks against its own people.
messages.United States of America: The United States, alongside the United Kingdom and France, acted lawfully, proportionally, and decisively to degrade Syria's chemical weapons capabilities and deter the Assad regime from further barbaric attacks against its own people. We categorically reject this draft resolution, which is an outrageous attempt to protect a regime that systematically uses weapons of mass destruction. We will not support any text that characterizes our defensive and humanitarian action as 'aggression'.

messages.Bolivia (Plurinational State of): Bolivia fully supports the draft resolution as presented. The unilateral military strikes conducted by the United States, France, and the United Kingdom constitute a flagrant violation of international law, the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic, and Article 2, paragraph 4 of the United Nations Charter. We stand ready to vote in favor of this text to defend multilateralism and the exclusive authority of the Security Council.
messages.China: China consistently opposes the use of force in international relations and advocates for strict adherence to the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations. Unilateral military actions conducted without the authorization of the Security Council violate international law and exacerbate tensions in the region. We fully support the draft resolution as drafted and stand ready to vote in favour.
messages.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire deeply regrets that the penholder has rejected all of our proposals aimed at achieving a balanced text. The current draft remains fundamentally one-sided by condemning the targeted strikes while completely ignoring the horrific chemical attack against civilians in Douma that triggered them. As our red lines have not been accommodated, Côte d’Ivoire cannot support this draft resolution in its current form.
messages.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea regrets that our previous proposals to achieve a balanced text were not accommodated. While we strictly uphold the principles of the UN Charter and the non-use of force without Security Council authorization, the Council must equally condemn the use of chemical weapons and prioritize de-escalation. In the absence of a balanced approach that addresses both the unauthorized strikes and the chemical weapons threat, our delegation cannot support this text and will be obliged to abstain.
messages.Ethiopia: Ethiopia regrets that our constructive proposals to bridge differences were not incorporated into this revision. Without language that balances respect for the UN Charter with an unequivocal condemnation of chemical weapons and a unified call for de-escalation, Ethiopia cannot support the text and will be obliged to abstain. We strongly encourage the penholder to seek a compromise text that reflects the collective responsibility of the Council.
messages.France: France categorically rejects this text, which seeks to condemn a necessary, proportionate, and targeted action conducted alongside the United States and the United Kingdom to degrade the Syrian regime's chemical weapons capabilities. Following the barbaric attack in Douma on 7 April, France could not tolerate the normalization of chemical weapons use in blatant violation of international law. As the penholder refuses to recognize the responsibility of the Syrian regime or address its repeated violations, France will vote against this draft resolution if put to a vote.
messages.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan shares grave concern over any military actions conducted without the authorization of the Security Council and underscores the urgent need for a thorough, impartial OPCW investigation into the events in Douma. However, as host of the Astana process and an advocate for de-escalation, Kazakhstan cannot endorse polarizing language that condemns Member States without Council consensus. If the draft cannot accommodate balanced language calling for maximum restraint and a political path forward, our delegation will not be in a position to support it and will abstain.
messages.Kuwait: Kuwait deeply regrets the penholder's refusal to reflect the horrific chemical weapons attack in Douma, which remains the root cause of the current escalation. While we consistently defend the United Nations Charter and international law regarding the use of force, a draft that ignores the prohibited use of chemical weapons against innocent civilians and focuses exclusively on condemning the strikes lacks necessary balance. In the absence of these essential modifications, Kuwait cannot support this draft and will abstain.
messages.Netherlands: The Netherlands cannot accept a draft resolution that condemns targeted and proportionate military action aimed at degrading Syria's chemical weapons capabilities while ignoring the atrocious chemical attack perpetrated in Douma. As host nation to the OPCW and a staunch defender of the international prohibition against chemical weapons, we insist that any Council product must address the root cause—the unacceptable use of chemical weapons—and ensure full accountability. If the text continues to condemn our allies and overlook the use of chemical weapons, the Netherlands will vote against it.
messages.Peru: Peru remains deeply committed to the principles of the United Nations Charter, international law, and the peaceful settlement of disputes, but we cannot support a draft resolution that completely ignores the abhorrent allegations of chemical weapons use in Douma. The Security Council must adopt a balanced approach that focuses on establishing the facts through the OPCW, creating an impartial attribution mechanism to ensure accountability, and avoiding one-sided condemnations. Without substantial modifications reflecting these priorities, Peru will not be able to vote in favor of this draft.
messages.Poland: Poland cannot accept a draft resolution that condemns the targeted and proportionate action taken by our allies to deter the Syrian regime from further use of chemical weapons. The text remains fundamentally unbalanced by ignoring the barbaric chemical attack against civilians in Douma that prompted this response. If the text remains in its current form, Poland will vote against it.
messages.Sweden: Sweden deeply regrets the penholder's refusal to accommodate our key concerns, resulting in a text that remains fundamentally unbalanced and unacceptable. The draft completely ignores the horrific chemical attack in Douma and inappropriate language characterizing the strikes as aggression cannot be accepted. If the draft remains in its current form without addressing these red lines, Sweden will vote against it.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom, alongside our French and American allies, took limited, targeted, and proportionate military action specifically directed at degrading the Syrian regime's chemical weapons capability and deterring their further barbaric use to alleviate extreme humanitarian suffering. This draft resolution willfully ignores the horrific chemical attack perpetrated against civilians in Douma and seeks to brand lawful humanitarian intervention as aggression. As our essential concerns have been flatly rejected by the penholder, the United Kingdom fundamentally opposes this text and will vote against it should it be tabled.
messages.United States of America: The United States unequivocally rejects this draft resolution, which cynically seeks to shield the murderous Assad regime from accountability for its abhorrent chemical weapons attack against innocent civilians in Douma. The targeted, legitimate, and proportionate military action undertaken by the United States, France, and the United Kingdom was necessary to degrade Syria's chemical weapons capabilities and deter further atrocities after Russia repeatedly paralyzed Council action. If this unacceptable and distorted text is brought to a vote, the United States will vote against it.

steps.summary: The Russian Federation firmly maintains the draft resolution in its current form to condemn the unprovoked, unlawful tripartite aggression against the Syrian Arab Republic. We categorically reject all attempts by the Western coalition and their allies to water down the text, legitimize the illegal use of force, and evade accountability under the United Nations Charter. The Council must fulfill its primary responsibility to uphold international law and defend the sovereignty of Member States.

reasons.China: China consistently opposes the use of force in international relations without the authorization of the Security Council, upholds the purposes and principles of the UN Charter, and firmly defends the sovereignty, independence, and territorial integrity of Syria.
reasons.Côte d’Ivoire: Côte d’Ivoire opposes the draft resolution because its essential red-line amendments—specifically the removal of language condemning the strikes by partner nations as an illegal aggression—were categorically rejected by the penholder, and Côte d’Ivoire maintains close diplomatic alignment with France and Western partners on chemical weapons non-proliferation.
reasons.Equatorial Guinea: Equatorial Guinea maintains a non-aligned, balanced position, upholding the principles of the UN Charter and sovereignty while also unequivocally opposing the use of chemical weapons. Since our proposed amendments to balance the text and remove one-sided condemnations were rejected by the penholder, we abstain on the draft resolution.
reasons.Ethiopia: Ethiopia abstains in line with its principled stance on adherence to the UN Charter, peaceful resolution of disputes, and opposition to both unauthorized military strikes and the use of chemical weapons, having seen its proposed balancing amendments rejected.
reasons.France: France conducted the targeted, legitimate, and proportionate strikes alongside the United States and the United Kingdom in response to the Syrian regime's heinous chemical weapons attack in Douma; we firmly reject this biased Russian draft resolution condemning our action.
reasons.Kazakhstan: Kazakhstan maintains a multi-vector foreign policy and balanced relations with both Russia and Western nations, prioritizing diplomatic dialogue, the Astana process, and restraint over polarization. Because our proposed amendments to soften the condemnatory language and emphasize political negotiation were rejected, Kazakhstan abstains in line with our consistent position.
reasons.Kuwait: Kuwait abstains because the draft resolution fails to condemn the horrific chemical weapons attack in Douma or address Syrian accountability, while also failing to bridge the divide among Council members or uphold a balanced approach consistent with Kuwait's regional foreign policy.
reasons.Netherlands: The Netherlands firmly rejects this unbalanced draft resolution, which ignores the horrific chemical weapons attack in Douma and seeks to condemn targeted and proportionate action taken by our allies to deter the Syrian regime from further use of chemical weapons.
reasons.Peru: Peru consistently condemns the use of chemical weapons and supports independent, multilateral investigation mechanisms, while upholding the UN Charter and the peaceful settlement of disputes. reasons.Russian Federation: As the sponsor of the draft resolution, the Russian Federation strongly supports condemning the unilateral military strikes launched by the United States, the United Kingdom, and France against Syria as an illegal act of aggression in violation of the UN Charter.
reasons.Sweden: Sweden opposes the draft resolution as it fails to address the horrific chemical weapons attack in Douma, disproportionately condemns the response by the United States, France, and the United Kingdom without acknowledging the context of repeated chemical weapons use by the Syrian regime, and rejected all of Sweden's core amendments.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom participated alongside the United States and France in targeted strikes against Syrian chemical weapons facilities following the Douma chemical attack; we firmly reject Russia's draft resolution condemning our lawful and proportionate humanitarian military action.
reasons.United States of America: The draft resolution directly condemns the joint US-UK-French military strikes against Syrian chemical weapons facilities and falsely brands our lawful, proportionate, and necessary response to Assad's chemical atrocities as aggression. The United States will resolutely vote against this hostile Russian text.

before.Bolivia (Plurinational State of):
Bolivia will vote in favour of the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. 

Our delegation vehemently and categorically condemns the unilateral military aggression carried out by the United States, the United Kingdom, and France against the territorial integrity and sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic. This unilateral armed action represents a flagrant, direct, and unacceptable violation of international law and the Charter of the United Nations, specifically Article 2, paragraph 4. 

The Security Council cannot become an instrument that rubber-stamps illegal unilateral actions or turns a blind eye when the fundamental principles of the international order are shredded. These military strikes were launched precisely when an independent, impartial OPCW Fact-Finding Mission was arriving on the ground in Syria to investigate the alleged chemical incident in Douma. Unilateral actions outside the framework of the United Nations undermine multilateralism and threaten international peace and security. For these principled reasons, Bolivia firmly supports this draft resolution.
before.Poland:
Poland will vote against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. 

The use of chemical weapons is an abhorrent violation of international law, international humanitarian law, and the Chemical Weapons Convention. The Syrian regime has repeatedly used chemical weapons against its own civilian population with complete impunity, most recently in Douma on 7 April, causing horrific suffering and dozens of tragic deaths, including women and children. 

The action taken overnight by the United States, the United Kingdom, and France was a direct, targeted, and proportionate response aimed specifically at deterring the further use of chemical weapons and degrading the Syrian regime’s chemical weapons capabilities. It was conducted in response to urgent humanitarian necessity following years of systematic blocking of the Security Council from upholding its responsibilities. 

The draft resolution before us completely ignores the root cause of the current situation—namely, the continued and heinous use of chemical weapons by the Assad regime and the failure of this Council to establish an independent accountability mechanism due to repeated vetoes. Poland stands firmly with our allies in upholding the global norm against the use of chemical weapons, and we therefore cannot support this text.
before.Russian Federation:
Mr. President,

Today is a black day in the history of the United Nations and of international relations. Last night, the United States, supported by the United Kingdom and France, carried out an act of blatant aggression against a sovereign State, the Syrian Arab Republic, in flagrant violation of the Charter of the United Nations, international law, and all accepted norms of inter-State conduct. 

This unprovoked strike was carried out on the basis of fabricated pretexts, bypassing the Security Council, at the very moment when experts from the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons were arriving in Damascus to conduct an impartial, on-site investigation into the alleged incident in Douma. Through their reckless actions, the troika of Western Powers has demonstrated utter contempt for international law and delivered a severe blow to the prospects for a peaceful political settlement in Syria. 

The Security Council cannot remain silent in the face of such neo-colonial hooliganism. We have submitted this draft resolution to unequivocally condemn this act of aggression, to demand an immediate end to the illegal use of force, and to uphold the fundamental principles of the United Nations Charter. We call on all responsible members of the Council to vote in favour of the draft resolution.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
The United Kingdom will vote against this draft resolution. 

Last Saturday, up to 75 people, including many children, were murdered in Douma in a horrific chemical weapons attack, and hundreds more suffered agonising injuries. All the indications are that the Syrian regime was responsible. The Syrian authorities have systematically used chemical weapons against their own people, in blatant violation of the Chemical Weapons Convention, resolution 2118 (2013), and international humanitarian law.

In response to this horrific atrocity, and following repeated Russian vetoes in this Council that blocked any diplomatic accountability mechanism, the United Kingdom, together with our French and American allies, took targeted and proportionate military action last night. Our action was specifically directed at degrading the Syrian regime’s chemical weapons capability and deterring their further use. It was legally justified on the basis of humanitarian intervention to alleviate extreme humanitarian distress. 

This draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation seeks to condemn action taken to uphold the international prohibition on the use of chemical weapons, while ignoring the grotesque chemical attacks perpetrated by the Syrian regime. It is cynical, self-serving, and completely detached from reality. We cannot and will not accept an attempt to brand action taken to alleviate civilian suffering and enforce the global ban on chemical weapons as an act of aggression. We urge all members of the Council to reject this draft resolution.
before.United States of America:
The United States, along with the United Kingdom and France, took targeted, proportionate, and legitimate action last night to deter the future use of chemical weapons by the Syrian regime. 

Just one week ago, the Assad regime unleashed chemical weapons on the innocent people of Douma, murdering dozens, including children, in a barbaric attack. Russia’s persistent vetoes have crippled this Council’s ability to uphold the international norm against the use of chemical weapons and shielded a murderous regime that gasses its own people. When the Security Council is repeatedly obstructed from acting, sovereign nations cannot stand by and allow the bedrock international consensus prohibiting the use of weapons of mass destruction to be shattered.

Our military action was carefully calibrated to degrade Syria’s chemical weapons research and development facilities and diminish its capacity to perpetrate further chemical attacks. We cannot and will not accept this cynical Russian draft resolution, which misrepresents the facts, seeks to whitewash Assad’s horrific war crimes, and falsely accuses those defending the international prohibition against chemical weapons of aggression. The United States will vote an emphatic "no."

after.China:
(spoke in Chinese): China has consistently stood for the peaceful settlement of disputes, opposed the use or threat of force in international relations, and advocated respect for the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of all countries. 

Any unilateral military action that bypasses the Security Council violates the purposes and principles of the Charter of the United Nations, as well as the basic principles and norms of international law, and will add new complicating factors to the settlement of the Syrian issue. China urges all parties concerned to refrain from any action that may escalate the situation, to return to the framework of international law, and to resolve the issue through dialogue and consultations.

China’s position on the issue of chemical weapons is consistent and clear: we consistently oppose the use of chemical weapons by any State, organization, or individual, under any circumstances, and for any purpose. China believes that a comprehensive, objective, and impartial investigation should be carried out into the suspected chemical attacks in Syria in order to reach a conclusion based on solid evidence and capable of withstanding the test of history. Pending the outcome of such an investigation, parties should not prejudge the outcome.

China believes that a political settlement is the only viable way out for the Syrian issue. The international community should continue to support the good offices of the United Nations, implement Security Council resolution 2254 (2015), and make unremitting efforts to facilitate a peaceful resolution of the Syrian conflict. 

Based on the principled position that I have just set out, China voted in favour of the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.
after.Côte d’Ivoire:
Mr. President,

My delegation voted against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Côte d’Ivoire reaffirms its categorical and unequivocal condemnation of the use of chemical weapons, by anyone, anywhere, and under any circumstances. Such acts constitute grave violations of international law, including international humanitarian law and the Chemical Weapons Convention, as well as an unacceptable threat to international peace and security. The horrifying scenes witnessed in Douma on 7 April, where dozens of civilians, including innocent women and children, lost their lives, cannot leave the international community indifferent.

My delegation was unable to support the draft resolution before us because it was deeply unbalanced. While it condemned the military strikes carried out overnight, it remained entirely silent on the horrific chemical attack that triggered this chain of events. A text that fails to address the very atrocity committed against civilians in Douma cannot serve as a credible or constructive basis for the Council’s action.

At the same time, Côte d’Ivoire remains deeply committed to the principles of the Charter of the United Nations, particularly the peaceful settlement of disputes, respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States, and the primary responsibility of the Security Council for the maintenance of international peace and security.

We call for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons Fact-Finding Mission to be granted full, safe, and unfettered access to Douma to establish the facts independently and objectively. Those responsible for the use of chemical weapons must be identified and held accountable for their heinous acts.

Finally, Côte d’Ivoire expresses its profound concern over the escalating tensions and urges all parties to exercise restraint. We appeal to the members of this Council, and particularly the permanent members, to overcome their divisions and unite around a revived political process. Only an inclusive political transition in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué can put an end to the prolonged tragedy endured by the Syrian people.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Equatorial Guinea:
Equatorial Guinea abstained in the voting on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, and I would like to explain our position.

The Republic of Equatorial Guinea views with grave concern the dangerous escalation of tensions and the military strikes carried out against the Syrian Arab Republic. Our country has always maintained a steadfast commitment to the principles enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations, particularly the peaceful settlement of disputes, respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of States, and the prohibition of the threat or use of force in international relations.

At the same time, Equatorial Guinea categorically condemns, in the strongest possible terms, the use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, and under any circumstances. Such heinous acts constitute a flagrant violation of international law, international humanitarian law, and the Chemical Weapons Convention, and those responsible must be held accountable.

In that regard, we reiterate our full support for the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW). We believe that an independent, impartial, and thorough investigation is indispensable to determine the facts on the ground regarding the alleged incident in Douma. Any unilateral military action undertaken prior to the conclusion of such an investigation undermines the collective multilateral framework that this Council is tasked with upholding.

Equatorial Guinea abstained on the draft resolution because we believe that the Security Council must avoid further polarization and work collectively to de-escalate tensions. What the Syrian people need most urgently is an immediate cessation of hostilities, unhindered humanitarian access, and a revitalized political process led by the United Nations, in line with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva communiqués. 

We urge all parties, both regional and international, to exercise maximum restraint, refrain from any action that could further destabilize the region or exacerbate the suffering of the civilian population, and commit themselves wholeheartedly to a peaceful and negotiated political solution to the conflict.
after.Ethiopia:
Ethiopia abstained in the voting on the draft resolution just considered by the Security Council. 

We would like to take this opportunity to explain the reasons for our vote and to reiterate our consistent, principled position on this very critical matter. 

First and foremost, Ethiopia reiterates its unequivocal condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by anyone, anywhere, under any circumstances. The use of such heinous weapons of mass destruction is a serious and unacceptable violation of international law, international humanitarian law, and the Chemical Weapons Convention. There can be no impunity for those responsible for such abhorrent acts. 

At the same time, we have consistently maintained that allegations concerning the use of chemical weapons must be verified through an independent, comprehensive, transparent, and impartial investigation. It is for this reason that we have supported the deployment of the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) to establish the facts regarding the alleged incident in Douma. Any conclusions and actions should be predicated on verified facts established through credible and impartial international mechanisms. 

Ethiopia is deeply concerned by the escalation of tensions and the military strikes carried out last night. At this extremely delicate and perilous juncture, military actions risk further aggravating an already devastating conflict, worsening the humanitarian catastrophe, and precipitating wider regional and international confrontation. 

We firmly believe that there is no military solution to the conflict in Syria. The only viable path forward is an inclusive, Syrian-led political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the 2012 Geneva communiqué. We call upon all parties to exercise maximum restraint, strictly respect the principles of the Charter of the United Nations and international law, and avoid any steps that could further derail diplomatic efforts. 

Finally, we urge the members of this Council, especially the permanent members, to overcome their divisions, bridge their differences, and work together in unity to uphold their collective responsibility under the Charter for the maintenance of international peace and security.
after.France:
*(spoke in French)*

Last night, forces of the French Republic, alongside those of the United States of America and the United Kingdom, carried out targeted military action against the clandestine chemical weapons capabilities of the Syrian regime.

This action was necessary, legitimate, and proportionate. It was conducted in full compliance with the goals and values of the Charter of the United Nations, to defend international law and the non-proliferation regime, and to prevent the Syrian regime from continuing to gas its own people with complete impunity.

On 7 April in Douma, a horrific chemical attack struck innocent civilians, killing dozens and injuring hundreds, including many women and children. The images of suffocation and suffering that shocked the conscience of the world left no doubt about the barbaric nature of this atrocity. Our own technical and intelligence assessments, made public this morning, established beyond any doubt the responsibility of the Syrian armed forces and security apparatus for this chemical strike.

For years, Bashar al-Assad's regime has flouted its international obligations under the Chemical Weapons Convention and resolution 2118 (2013), which this Council adopted unanimously. It has turned weapons of mass destruction into an instrument of terror against its own population. Confronted with these repeated, documented crimes, this Council has unfortunately been paralyzed. Russia has systematically shielded the Syrian regime and blocked any meaningful Council action, using its veto repeatedly—most recently to terminate the Joint Investigative Mechanism and to prevent the creation of a new, independent attribution mechanism. 

Faced with this persistent paralysis and the blatant violation of one of the most fundamental norms of the international order—the absolute prohibition on the use of chemical weapons—our nations could not stand idly by. To do nothing would have been to accept the normalization of the use of chemical weapons, creating an intolerable precedent for global security.

Our strikes were strictly limited. They targeted three specific sites directly linked to the Syrian regime’s chemical weapons program—a research center and two production and storage sites. They were meticulously planned and executed to destroy the regime’s capacity to manufacture and employ chemical weapons, while avoiding civilian casualties and any escalation with other actors on the ground. 

France voted resolutely against the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation. That draft did nothing to address the reality of chemical weapons use by the Syrian regime, nor did it offer any path forward. Instead, it sought to condemn those who stepped in to uphold the international non-proliferation regime that this Council was prevented from defending.

Our collective responsibility does not end with these strikes; on the contrary, our political and diplomatic work must now accelerate. The international community must unite around three urgent priorities:

First, on chemical weapons, we must ensure the complete, verifiable dismantling of the Syrian chemical program and establish a permanent, independent attribution mechanism to identify and hold accountable all perpetrators of chemical attacks. The Fact-Finding Mission of the OPCW must also be granted full, unhindered access to Douma immediately.

Second, on the humanitarian front, we must secure full and unhindered humanitarian access throughout Syrian territory and implement a genuine, nationwide ceasefire in accordance with resolution 2401 (2018).

Third, on the political track, there is no military solution to the Syrian crisis. Only an inclusive, credible political transition, led under United Nations auspices in Geneva in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015), can bring lasting peace to Syria and the region.

To this end, France, together with its American and British partners, will present a comprehensive draft resolution to the Security Council addressing these three dimensions: chemical, humanitarian, and political. We call on all members of the Council, without exception, to join us in overcoming past divisions and assuming our shared responsibility for international peace and security.
after.Kazakhstan:
Kazakhstan abstained in the voting on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation.

Kazakhstan expresses its grave concern over the further escalation of the situation in the Syrian Arab Republic and the military strikes carried out on its territory. We believe that military action undermines efforts to achieve a peaceful and lasting political settlement to the Syrian crisis. 

Kazakhstan’s position on the Syrian conflict has been consistent and principled. We firmly believe that there is no military solution to the crisis and that a political resolution can be achieved only through peaceful negotiations and constructive dialogue, in accordance with the Charter of the United Nations, relevant Security Council resolutions, particularly resolution 2254 (2015), and the norms of international law. We reaffirm our full support for the Geneva process under the auspices of the United Nations, as well as the Astana process, which has contributed to reducing violence and establishing de-escalation zones.

Kazakhstan reiterates its categorical condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any party, anywhere, and under any circumstances. The use of weapons of mass destruction is unacceptable and constitutes a gross violation of international law. We emphasize that any allegations of the use of chemical weapons must be thoroughly, professionally, objectively, and impartially investigated by the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, and that those responsible must be identified and held accountable.

At this critical and dangerous juncture, we call on all parties concerned to exercise maximum restraint, prevent any further escalation or military confrontation, and respect the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic. We urge the members of the Security Council to overcome divisions, demonstrate collective responsibility, and work together in unity to preserve international peace and security.
after.Kuwait:
Mr. President,

The State of Kuwait abstained from voting on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, and I wish to explain the reasons for our vote.

First and foremost, the State of Kuwait reaffirms its principled and unwavering position condemning in the strongest possible terms the use of chemical weapons by any party, under any circumstances, anywhere in the world. The use of such weapons is a heinous crime, an intolerable violation of international law and international humanitarian law, and a blatant contravention of the Chemical Weapons Convention and relevant Security Council resolutions, particularly resolution 2118 (2013). Those responsible for the use of such horrific weapons must be held fully accountable and brought to justice, so that impunity does not prevail.

In this regard, we express our profound regret that the Security Council was unable earlier this week to shoulder its primary responsibility under the Charter of the United Nations for the maintenance of international peace and security, and failed to agree on the establishment of an independent, impartial, and professional international mechanism to investigate and identify the perpetrators of chemical attacks in the Syrian Arab Republic. The persistent division within the Council has prevented it from taking unified and decisive action to address these grave crimes.

At the same time, the State of Kuwait reiterates the vital importance of strict adherence to international law and the Charter of the United Nations, particularly the principles of respecting the sovereignty, independence, unity, and territorial integrity of all States. We support the efforts of the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons, which has arrived in Syria, and we urge all parties to provide it with full, immediate, and unhindered access to conduct a thorough and transparent investigation into the alleged incident in Douma.

Finally, we reiterate our conviction that there can be no military solution to the Syrian crisis. Sustainable peace and stability can only be achieved through an inclusive, Syrian-led political process that meets the legitimate aspirations of the Syrian people, in accordance with the Geneva Communiqué of 2012 and Security Council resolution 2254 (2015).

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Netherlands:
Mr. President,

The Kingdom of the Netherlands voted against the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. 

The draft resolution was completely one-sided. It deliberately ignored the horrific events in Douma on 7 April, where chemical weapons were once again used against innocent civilians, including women and children. The use of chemical weapons is a war crime, a gross violation of international law, and an unacceptable threat to international peace and security. It cannot and must not go unanswered. 

The Security Council bears the primary responsibility for the maintenance of international peace and security. Yet, this Council has repeatedly been paralyzed. Earlier this week, a draft resolution to establish an independent, impartial mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical attacks in Syria was blocked by a veto. In the face of repeated vetoes shielding the Syrian regime, the Council was prevented from upholding the fundamental international norm prohibiting the use of weapons of mass destruction.

Under these exceptional circumstances, the targeted, calibrated, and proportionate military action taken overnight by France, the United Kingdom, and the United States was understandable. Its sole purpose was to deter the Syrian regime from the further horrific use of chemical weapons and to degrade its chemical capabilities. 

We now urgently call for the OPCW Fact-Finding Mission, whose experts have arrived in Damascus, to be granted immediate, safe, and unfettered access to all relevant sites in Douma without delay or interference. Accountability is essential; impunity for the use of chemical weapons cannot be tolerated, and perpetrators must be held responsible.

Finally, there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria. We urge all members of this Council, and particularly the Russian Federation, to use their influence to bring an end to the violence and genuinely engage in a UN-led political process in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué.

I thank you, Mr. President.
after.Peru:
Peru abstained in the voting on the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, and I wish to explain the reasons for our vote.

Peru reiterates its firm and principled rejection and condemnation of the use of chemical weapons by any actor, anywhere, and under any circumstances. Such acts constitute grave violations of international law, international humanitarian law, and the Chemical Weapons Convention, and can constitute war crimes. In this regard, we express our profound concern over the alleged chemical weapons attack in Douma on 7 April, which resulted in the loss of innocent civilian lives, including many women and children.

We reiterate our full support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons (OPCW) and its Fact-Finding Mission, and we emphasize the importance of allowing its experts to carry out their work in an independent, objective, and unimpeded manner to determine the facts. At the same time, Peru deeply regrets that the Security Council was unable earlier this week to establish an independent and impartial attribution mechanism to identify those responsible for the use of chemical weapons in the Syrian Arab Republic and ensure accountability.

Peru firmly believes that any measures taken to maintain or restore international peace and security must strictly adhere to the Charter of the United Nations and international law. We are deeply concerned by the escalation of military actions, which risks further destabilizing an already fragile region and exacerbating the immense suffering of the Syrian people.

We abstained on the draft resolution because its text was not balanced and did not adequately reflect the gravity of the events or the context that led to this situation, including the repeated use of chemical weapons and the paralysis of this Council. 

Peru calls on all parties to exercise maximum restraint and avoid any actions that could escalate tensions. We reaffirm our conviction that there can be no military solution to the conflict in Syria, and that the only viable path to lasting peace is through a Syrian-led, Syrian-owned political process facilitated by the United Nations, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the Geneva Communiqué.
after.Russian Federation:
(spoke in Russian):

We regret that the Security Council was unable to adopt the draft resolution submitted by the Russian Federation, which was aimed at defending the fundamental principles of international law and the Charter of the United Nations. 

Today, the mask has completely slipped. The vote on our draft resolution clearly demonstrated who stands for international law, the peaceful settlement of disputes, and the supremacy of the United Nations Charter, and who prefers brute force, military adventurism, and unilateral diktat. 

The three permanent members of the Security Council—the United States, the United Kingdom, and France—along with their allies who voted against our resolution, have demonstrated utter contempt for international law and for the Security Council itself. By attempting to justify their unprovoked aggression with hypocritical rhetoric about humanitarian concerns, they have dealt a severe blow to the system of international relations established after the Second World War.

Let us be completely frank about what occurred last night: under the fabricated pretext of a staged chemical incident in Douma, the Western troika launched missile strikes against a sovereign State at the exact moment when the Fact-Finding Mission of the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons was arriving in Damascus to conduct an impartial, on-site investigation. If you were genuinely interested in establishing the truth, why did you not wait even twenty-four hours for the inspectors to do their work? The answer is obvious: you were terrified that an objective investigation would demolish your lies and expose the entire pretext as a blatant provocation orchestrated by terrorists and their patrons.

Moreover, the targets struck were scientific research centres and civilian facilities that had already been inspected by the OPCW and certified as having no connection to chemical weapons activities. By striking these sites, you not only violated the sovereignty of the Syrian Arab Republic, but you directly undermined the OPCW and the international non-proliferation regime.

We have also heard belligerent statements in this chamber today, including the assertion that the United States remains “locked and loaded” to strike again. We strongly urge Washington, London, and Paris to immediately tone down their aggressive rhetoric, renounce their dangerous neo-colonial habits, and refrain from any further reckless actions that threaten international peace and security. The international community cannot be held hostage to the geopolitical ambitions and cowboy diplomacy of a handful of Western capitals.

Russia will continue to resolutely defend the Charter of the United Nations, uphold the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Syrian Arab Republic, and work towards a genuine political settlement in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015).
after.Sweden:
Sweden voted against the draft resolution presented by the Russian Federation. 

We did so because the draft resolution was deeply unbalanced. It completely ignored the horrific chemical weapons attack carried out in Douma on 7 April, which killed and injured dozens of innocent civilians, including children. To condemn the military response while remaining silent on the atrocity that triggered it is unacceptable.

Sweden’s position has always been guided by a firm and principled commitment to international law and the Charter of the United Nations. The prohibition of the use of chemical weapons is absolute, and any use of these abhorrent weapons constitutes a grave violation of international law and international humanitarian law. There can be no impunity for such war crimes; those responsible must be held accountable.

It is deeply regrettable that this Council has once again failed to shoulder its responsibility under the Charter. Earlier this week, the Council was blocked from establishing an independent, impartial, and professional attribution mechanism to identify the perpetrators of chemical attacks in Syria. When the Council fails to act in the face of the repeated use of weapons of mass destruction, it damages the credibility of the entire multilateral system and undermines the rules-based international order.

At the same time, Sweden is deeply concerned about the risk of further military escalation, which would only exacerbate the immense suffering of the Syrian people. We call on all parties to exercise maximum restraint and to avoid any actions that could destabilize the situation further. 

We underline our full support for the Organisation for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons and its Fact-Finding Mission, which must be granted immediate, full, and unhindered access to the site in Douma to conduct its investigation without delay or interference. 

Finally, let us be clear: there is no military solution to the conflict in Syria. The only path forward is an inclusive, Syrian-led political process under United Nations auspices, in accordance with resolution 2254 (2015) and the 2012 Geneva communiqué. We urge all members of this Council, and in particular its permanent members, to set aside their divisions and genuinely unite to revitalize the UN-led political process.
